claims.statement: The dashboard backend is an APIRouter with prefix "/dashboard/api" and a router-level mutation-origin dependency; agent/api/app.py includes it and then invokes mount_dashboard_ui(app).

agent/dashboard/__init__.py exposes the router lazily via a PEP 562 __getattr__ so that importing a dashboard submodule does not drag in routes.py, FastAPI, and every API/job module; only the webapp that mounts the router pays that import cost.

GitHub login issues signed state carrying a hashed nonce stored in a short-lived state cookie and redirects to GitHub; the normal callback validates it, exchanges the code, enforces the organization gate, persists the token, and issues a signed session cookie, while a desktop handoff returns a PKCE-bound code without setting that browser cookie.

Session cookie flags derive from the API scheme and whether dashboard and API are same-origin: HTTP is non-Secure SameSite=Lax, same-origin HTTPS is Secure SameSite=Lax, and split-origin HTTPS is Secure SameSite=None.

Every dashboard mutation is guarded by the router-level require_same_origin_for_mutations dependency, which passes GET/HEAD/OPTIONS and bearer-token-only requests but rejects cookie-authenticated mutations whose Origin/Referer is not allowed; WebSockets always receive the origin check.

In deployed builds ui/server/backend-proxy.ts is the Nitro handler for /dashboard/api/** and /webhooks/**, reads DASHBOARD_API_URL per request, keeps OAuth 3xx hops with redirect: "manual", and fails if DASHBOARD_API_URL is unset rather than using a production backend default.

During SSR the dashboard fetch layer copies the incoming request's cookie header onto forwarded requests because credentials: "include" is meaningless on the server, and it targets DASHBOARD_API_URL directly instead of a relative origin.
Electron’s BackendSupervisor lazily starts a token-authenticated loopback LangGraph server on 127.0.0.1 from langgraph.desktop.json in development or the bundled configuration when packaged.

The local-graph proxy removes renderer cookies, injects the supervisor's random bearer token, and exposes the stable /local-graph agent configuration; startup polls that authenticated loopback server, while shutdown escalates from SIGTERM to SIGKILL after its timeout.

The Agents UI permits an unauthenticated desktop-local-only session only on the root or /agents/local/ routes; its shared stream provider selects local transport for a local session and cloud transport otherwise.

The backend dashboard UI mount serves a configured or in-repository static build at the root, gives hashed assets immutable caching and the shell no-cache, declines reserved server paths and non-HTML unknown paths, and can instead reverse-proxy a Vite dev server while keeping the backend origin.
The dashboard UI catch-all must be registered after API routes; keep_dashboard_ui_last moves it behind subsequently registered routes.
At application construction, DASHBOARD_ALLOWED_ORIGINS configures credentialed CORS, but a wildcard origin is rejected because credentials are enabled.

dashboard/routes.py is an aggregation boundary that includes feature-owned routers, including authentication, profiles, workspace settings, repositories, reviews, skills, schedules, threads, incidents, and workspaces, beneath the common dashboard prefix.

Dashboard thread routes expose guarded state, command, history, and SSE event paths; event streaming preflights JSON content type and readability before the response starts, then proxies LangGraph events as text/event-stream.

The dashboard command proxy permits a missing thread only for run.start, enriches the command before forwarding it, stamps successful starts as pending, and asynchronously observes the run for time-to-first assistant text.

AgentStreamProvider uses dashboard versus local graph clients by transport, retains recently left and running streams in a pool, invalidates cloud thread queries at completion, and surfaces custom offloading and model-routing events.

Profiles keep user-editable settings and encrypted OAuth tokens in separate namespaces to avoid concurrent profile edits and OAuth token refreshes overwriting each other, and profile validation rejects unsupported default model and reasoning-effort pairs.
Workspace settings resolve hardcoded defaults, an instance record, and sparse workspace overrides; they validate model pairs and derive valid supported model defaults and feature-toggle behavior.
Agent-instruction records normalize repository names and require current repository access for direct operations, and return non-empty stored instruction text for prompt assembly.

Personal skills are authenticated-user scoped, organization skills are readable by any session and writable only by administrators, and schedule listing is session-protected while schedule mutations require administration.
The deployed backend proxy filters hop-by-hop and reframed response headers and preserves each upstream Set-Cookie as a separate header.

The focused dashboard thread tests verify run-start metadata and TTFT observation, reject unsurfaced or unauthorized protected-thread commands, allow readable non-owner state/event/history access, and cap unscoped history discovery.
